subject: chopperMotorbike
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: custom chopper motorbike.
Style: Overwatch.
reasoning:
I'm designing a custom chopper in an Overwatch-inspired style—bold stylized shapes, clean colors, glowing orange/teal accents, hard-surface paneling. Since it's a vehicle rather than a creature, I just need one root joint named "body" to satisfy the single-root requirement.

I'm planning the wheel joints for rigging and working out the geometry: a 2.4m long chopper with raked front fork, rear wheel radius 0.38 and front wheel radius 0.36, using safe builder APIs like lathe, sweep, and extrude. I'm calculating the fork angle and axle positions, then sketching the tire cross-section as a lathe profile around the X axis to get a rounded torus-like shape for the wheels.

Setting up the joint hierarchy next: frame root, fork joint aiming at the front axle, wheelF parented to fork, wheelR parented to frame, with handlebars on the fork joint. I'll add a rod helper for connecting two points with a radius for building the fork tubes and frame struts, then start laying out parts—beginning with the V-twin engine block, angled cylinders with cooling fins, and covers positioned near the frame center.

Defining tank loft stations...

Working out the rear fender geometry...

Setting the fender section radius with a small box profile aligned to the path's binormal, then moving on to frame geometry—backbone rod from head to seat post, rear struts connecting engine to axle on each side, and seat stay rods tying into the same rear mounting points.

I'm placing a lathe-turned bullet headlight with a glow lens mounted at the fork front, then building ape-hanger handlebars as a Catmull-Rom sweep rising from the center grip outward and upward on each side, plus small mirror tubes and risers. For the front wheel I'm planning a dark tire, steel rim with an orange glowing hub disc, and spokes using a similar sweep technique.

I realize the sidewall stripe plane would end up hidden inside the tire's solid cross-section since the lathe forms a closed loop between the inner and outer radius across the tire's full width, so I need to rethink where the plane actually needs to sit to be visible.

I'll place the sidewall disc just outside the tire face, offset slightly to avoid z-fighting, sized to cover the rim-to-sidewall region while leaving the inner hub area hollow so the rim shows through.

For other details I'm adding a hub cylinder with a protruding axle stub on each side, a glowing ring accent, plus mechanical extras like a rear sprocket disc, a simple chain/belt loop, and foot pegs as small cylinders. For the Overwatch-style flavor, I want a glowing teal energy strip under the frame, holographic underglow, hex decals, and orange-gray color blocks possibly with hazard striping.

Now I'm adding glow details: headlight, red tail light, teal strips along the fork and tank, and an engine core glowing ring like a Tesla coil. For the base, I'm considering an octagonal low platform with hex-pattern texture and a glow ring, and need to account for the bike's wheels resting on top of that platform rather than at floor level — so I'll define a base height offset constant and shift the bike's position so everything still appears to rest at floor level.

Let me simplify by just defining a small ground offset constant and adding it uniformly to all height values, rather than messing with root translation which feels risky given how the rig might be baked.

Writing base lathe profile...

For props, I'm thinking of adding a glowing hexagonal pad under the bike, a red tool chest with a wrench, an oil drum with hazard stripes near the rear, and a spare tire stack to fill out the scene. I'll also add a small rear license plate reading "OW-76" as a decorative detail.

I need to plan out several textures: wheel face, tank emblem, license plate, a small speedo gauge, a hex badge, hazard stripes for the drum, and crate markings. For the paint style, I want a cel-shaded look with warm highlights on top and cool shading on the bottom, so I'll write a helper function using mix and rgb to blend colors based on surface normal direction before importing the needed SDK utilities and writing the actual code.

Defining color palette and tone helper...

Now I'm setting up the chopper builder itself, starting with the frame joint and the fork joint positioned at the head with a hinge role for steering.

Defining wheel joints...

Still writing wheel geometry...

Now I'm working out the fork geometry — computing mirrored tube positions from the triple tree down to the axle, figuring the rake angle, and splitting each fork leg into a thicker steel upper sleeve and a chrome lower slider.

Modeling the headlight bucket with a lathe shape, building a profile that curves outward then narrows toward a flat front face for the lens.

Working out where the fork tubes meet to position the headlight between them, adjusting its radius and the fork spread so the lamp sits properly without clashing against the tubes.

Now I'm designing the ape-hanger handlebars rising from the triple tree, plotting a curved path from the risers up and back toward the rider with grips positioned at the path's end.

I'll add a brake lever, small mirrors, and a simple speedometer gauge mounted near the triple tree facing backward. Then I'm moving on to the frame and engine block, placing the crankcase at the bike's center with box geometry for the main body.

Now I'm shaping the V-twin cylinders with angled directions for front and rear, adding cooling fins as stacked discs along each cylinder, dome-shaped cylinder heads, rocker covers, and finally an air cleaner intake with a chrome housing and glowing accent ring mounted to the side of the engine.

Still mapping exhaust pipe paths...

Skipping the clamps for simplicity, I'll just add a glowing disc at the pipe tip instead. Then I'm moving to the tank loft, setting up stations with the correct paint color and dimensions, positioning it on the backbone, and placing a decal on its surface using a computed surface hit point.

For the decal placement I need to find the right hit point around the tank's surface with a guard in case nothing is found, and I'm also adding two symmetric teal glow strips along the tank using angled sweep lines on either side.

Now I'm placing the rear fender details: a small glowing red taillight box and a license plate plane tilted to face backward at the fender's end, with the fender arc endpoint calculated at a -30° angle to get its low position in y and z.

I'm sitting the seat just above the rear fender, positioning it low and slightly forward with stations spanning roughly z=-.75 to -.1, raising from y.86 near the fender top to a mid-peak around .98.

I'm now laying out the frame geometry: the backbone running back from the head area under the tank, lower engine rails extending to the rear axle area, seat stays bracing from the seat down to the rear rail junction, and the downtube dropping from the head.

Still working out the drive-train details -- placing the rear wheel sprocket and belt/chain rods connecting it to the engine output sprocket, approximating the chain run with a couple of connecting rods between the two sprocket positions.

Now I'm adding footpegs as small cylinders mounted along the x-axis near the engine, plus a kickstand rod angled down to the ground and foot plate boxes. I'm deciding to skip rear shocks since this is a hardtail frame.

Then I'm placing an oil tank cylinder under the seat on the left side with a teal glow band, a battery box on the right, and considering Overwatch-style flourishes like glowing hard-light aero fins or twin orange tail fins mounted on a sissy bar behind the seat.

Still writing fin geometry... adding a padded backrest outline and chrome sissy bar rods extending up from the rear seat points.

I'm placing a glowing teal underbody strip beneath the engine as an underglow effect, plus small tire-level light strips and a wider glow bar underneath, all set to a stronger glow intensity. For the front, I'm adding small teal glow rings positioned along the lower fork tubes.

Now I'm moving to the base and structural pieces, defining the base using a lathed profile with eight segments attached to the root frame joint since it doesn't need to move with steering. I'm shaping the base profile to span the bike's length, covering from the front wheel area back along the frame.

Still defining base geometry...

I'm adding a glowing teal rim sweep around the inset top edge using a closed chamfered-rect polyline, accepting slight corner cap overlap for simplicity. Now I'm planning a prop oil drum near the base corner—a short hazard-striped cylinder—deciding to paint the stripes procedurally rather than texture-map them.

I'll make the drum body navy with a yellow-and-black hazard stripe ring near the top, add a small red toolbox with a handle and wrench rods nearby, and skip the spare tire in favor of a glowing hex-prism charging pad pylon at the front-left corner.

For the tank's emblem, I'm thinking a white circle with a navy ring, a chevron bar through the middle, a small dot accent, and maybe a bold italic "76" to give it that stenciled insignia look.

I'm deciding the decal doesn't need mirroring on either side since it's drawn facing the viewer and reads correctly undistorted. For the gauge, a simple circle with tick marks will do, and I'll skip the handlebar detail to keep things reasonable at around 120 parts total.

Now I'm working out the fender sweep geometry -- defining a radius function and arc parameters based on the rear wheel center, calculating the start point and rotation angle so the fender clears the tire with the right offset.

Checking the rotated positions: at 90 degrees the fender top sits at the expected point above the wheel, and at 105 degrees it curves forward to meet near the seat's starting edge, with enough gap between fender and seat. I'm also placing the taillight glow box near the fender tip and planning a license plate below it.

Now I'm working out the fork geometry, aligning the tube endpoints from the head tube down to the front axle so the rake angle stays consistent rather than drifting off-line.

Still placing headlight and fork geometry...

For the hub, I'm deciding against making the whole wheel glow since that'd flatten the neon effect -- instead I'll add a separate thin teal ring with its own glow applied, positioned just outside the main rim radius, built as a lathe shape around the wheel's axis.

Checking the lathe axis orientation and tire UV painting setup, then confirming color definitions stay compact since paints are separate. I'm defining a chrome paint that mixes colors based on surface normal with noise variation for a metallic look.

Still writing geometry...

I'm adding a ring of bolts using trigonometry for placement, confirming the rod helper signature, setting up gauge and plate geometries, and designing a license plate SVG with a navy border and "OW-76" text before finalizing the answer.
